question: Why do some imported canvas trainers have a thin layer of fabric glued to the sole?
answer: To be taxed as a lower-duty kind of shoe. US tariffs classify footwear by the material of the outer sole that touches the ground, and rubber-soled canvas shoes pay far more than ones soled in textile. A felt skin over most of the tread wears off within days, but it counts at the border.
move: When a product has a strange detail, check the rulebook it was designed around.
ask: What odd detail in something I own might be there just to dodge a rule?
reference: US International Trade Commission, Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States, Chapter 64: Footwear, 2024
